/-- `a * a⁻¹` is idempotent. -/
theorem isIdempotentElem_mul_inv (a : S) : IsIdempotentElem (a * a⁻¹) :=
  show a * a⁻¹ * (a * a⁻¹) = a * a⁻¹ by
    rw [← mul_assoc, mul_inv_mul]

/-- `a⁻¹ * a` is idempotent. -/
theorem isIdempotentElem_inv_mul (a : S) : IsIdempotentElem (a⁻¹ * a) :=
  show a⁻¹ * a * (a⁻¹ * a) = a⁻¹ * a by
    rw [← mul_assoc, inv_mul_inv]

/-- An idempotent is its own inverse. -/
theorem inv_idem {e : S} (he : IsIdempotentElem e) : e⁻¹ = e := by
  have h : e * e * e = e := by rw [he.eq, he.eq]
  exact (inv_unique h h).symm

/-- The product of two idempotents is idempotent (Howie, Thm 5.1.1, first
half): with `x := (e * f)⁻¹`, the element `f * x * e` is an idempotent
inverse of `e * f`, so `x = f * x * e` by uniqueness, `x` is idempotent, and
`e * f = x⁻¹ = x`. -/
theorem isIdempotentElem_mul {e f : S} (he : IsIdempotentElem e)
    (hf : IsIdempotentElem f) : IsIdempotentElem (e * f) := by
  obtain ⟨x, hx⟩ : ∃ x : S, x = (e * f)⁻¹ := ⟨_, rfl⟩
  have he2 : ∀ z : S, e * (e * z) = e * z := fun z => by rw [← mul_assoc, he.eq]
  have hf2 : ∀ z : S, f * (f * z) = f * z := fun z => by rw [← mul_assoc, hf.eq]
  have hx1 : (e * f) * x * (e * f) = e * f := by rw [hx]; exact mul_inv_mul (e * f)
  have hx2 : ∀ z : S, x * (e * (f * (x * z))) = x * z := fun z => by
    have h := congrArg (· * z) (inv_mul_inv (e * f))
    rw [← hx] at h
    simpa only [mul_assoc] using h
  -- `f * x * e` is an inverse of `e * f` ...
  have hA : (e * f) * (f * x * e) * (e * f) = e * f := by
    have h := hx1
    simp only [mul_assoc] at h ⊢
    rw [hf2, he2]
    exact h
  have hB : (f * x * e) * (e * f) * (f * x * e) = f * x * e := by
    simp only [mul_assoc]
    rw [he2, hf2, hx2]
  -- ... so it equals `x` by uniqueness, and hence `x` is idempotent
  have hxeq : f * x * e = x := (inv_unique hA hB).trans hx.symm
  have hxx : IsIdempotentElem x := by
    have h : (f * x * e) * (f * x * e) = f * x * e := by
      simp only [mul_assoc]
      rw [hx2]
    rw [hxeq] at h
    exact h
  -- finally `e * f = x⁻¹ = x` is idempotent
  have hef : e * f = x := by
    have h := inv_idem hxx
    rw [hx, inv_inv] at h
    rw [hx]
    exact h
  rw [hef]
  exact hxx

/-- **Idempotents commute.**  This is the crux of inverse semigroup theory:
a regular semigroup has unique inverses iff its idempotents commute.

Proof (Howie, Thm 5.1.1): both `e * f` and `f * e` are idempotent by
`isIdempotentElem_mul`, and each is then an inverse of the other, so
uniqueness gives `f * e = (e * f)⁻¹ = e * f`. -/
theorem idempotent_mul_comm {e f : S} (he : IsIdempotentElem e)
    (hf : IsIdempotentElem f) : e * f = f * e := by
  have hef := isIdempotentElem_mul he hf
  have hfe := isIdempotentElem_mul hf he
  have he2 : ∀ z : S, e * (e * z) = e * z := fun z => by rw [← mul_assoc, he.eq]
  have hf2 : ∀ z : S, f * (f * z) = f * z := fun z => by rw [← mul_assoc, hf.eq]
  have hA : (e * f) * (f * e) * (e * f) = e * f := by
    have h := hef.eq
    simp only [mul_assoc] at h ⊢
    rw [hf2, he2]
    exact h
  have hB : (f * e) * (e * f) * (f * e) = f * e := by
    have h := hfe.eq
    simp only [mul_assoc] at h ⊢
    rw [he2, hf2]
    exact h
  exact ((inv_unique hA hB).trans (inv_idem hef)).symm

theorem isIdempotentElem_mul_inv (a : S) : IsIdempotentElem (a * a⁻¹) :=
  show a * a⁻¹ * (a * a⁻¹) = a * a⁻¹ by
    rw [← mul_assoc, mul_inv_mul]

/-- `a⁻¹ * a` is idempotent. -/

  show a⁻¹ * a * (a⁻¹ * a) = a⁻¹ * a by
    rw [← mul_assoc, inv_mul_inv]

/-- An idempotent is its own inverse. -/
theorem inv_idem {e : S} (he : IsIdempotentElem e) : e⁻¹ = e := by
  have h : e * e * e = e := by rw [he.eq, he.eq]
  exact (inv_unique h h).symm

/-- The product of two idempotents is idempotent (Howie, Thm 5.1.1, first
half): with `x := (e * f)⁻¹`, the element `f * x * e` is an idempotent
inverse of `e * f`, so `x = f * x * e` by uniqueness, `x` is idempotent, and
`e * f = x⁻¹ = x`. -/
theorem isIdempotentElem_mul {e f : S} (he : IsIdempotentElem e)
    (hf : IsIdempotentElem f) : IsIdempotentElem (e * f) := by
  obtain ⟨x, hx⟩ : ∃ x : S, x = (e * f)⁻¹ := ⟨_, rfl⟩
  have he2 : ∀ z : S, e * (e * z) = e * z := fun z => by rw [← mul_assoc, he.eq]
  have hf2 : ∀ z : S, f * (f * z) = f * z := fun z => by rw [← mul_assoc, hf.eq]
  have hx1 : (e * f) * x * (e * f) = e * f := by rw [hx]; exact mul_inv_mul (e * f)
  have hx2 : ∀ z : S, x * (e * (f * (x * z))) = x * z := fun z => by
    have h := congrArg (· * z) (inv_mul_inv (e * f))
    rw [← hx] at h
    simpa only [mul_assoc] using h
  -- `f * x * e` is an inverse of `e * f` ...
  have hA : (e * f) * (f * x * e) * (e * f) = e * f := by
    have h := hx1
    simp only [mul_assoc] at h ⊢
    rw [hf2, he2]
    exact h
  have hB : (f * x * e) * (e * f) * (f * x * e) = f * x * e := by
    simp only [mul_assoc]
    rw [he2, hf2, hx2]
  -- ... so it equals `x` by uniqueness, and hence `x` is idempotent
  have hxeq : f * x * e = x := (inv_unique hA hB).trans hx.symm
  have hxx : IsIdempotentElem x := by
    have h : (f * x * e) * (f * x * e) = f * x * e := by
      simp only [mul_assoc]
      rw [hx2]
    rw [hxeq] at h
    exact h

  have hef : e * f = x := by
    have h := inv_idem hxx
    rw [hx, inv_inv] at h
    rw [hx]
    exact h
  rw [hef]

uniqueness gives `f * e = (e * f)⁻¹ = e * f`. -/

  have hef := isIdempotentElem_mul he hf
  have hfe := isIdempotentElem_mul hf he
  have he2 : ∀ z : S, e * (e * z) = e * z := fun z => by rw [← mul_assoc, he.eq]
  have hf2 : ∀ z : S, f * (f * z) = f * z := fun z => by rw [← mul_assoc, hf.eq]
  have hA : (e * f) * (f * e) * (e * f) = e * f := by
    have h := hef.eq
    simp only [mul_assoc] at h ⊢
    rw [hf2, he2]
    exact h
  have hB : (f * e) * (e * f) * (f * e) = f * e := by
    have h := hfe.eq
    simp only [mul_assoc] at h ⊢
    rw [he2, hf2]
    exact h
  exact ((inv_unique hA hB).trans (inv_idem hef)).symm

/-- The inverse of a product: `b⁻¹ * a⁻¹` is an inverse of `a * b` (sliding
the idempotents `b * b⁻¹` and `a⁻¹ * a` past each other with
`idempotent_mul_comm`), so it is *the* inverse by `inv_unique`. -/
theorem mul_inv_rev (a b : S) : (a * b)⁻¹ = b⁻¹ * a⁻¹ := by
  have hcomm := idempotent_mul_comm (isIdempotentElem_mul_inv b) (isIdempotentElem_inv_mul a)
  have h1 : (a * b) * (b⁻¹ * a⁻¹) * (a * b) = a * b :=
    calc (a * b) * (b⁻¹ * a⁻¹) * (a * b)
        = a * ((b * b⁻¹) * (a⁻¹ * a)) * b := by simp only [mul_assoc]
      _ = a * ((a⁻¹ * a) * (b * b⁻¹)) * b := by rw [hcomm]
      _ = (a * a⁻¹ * a) * (b * b⁻¹ * b) := by simp only [mul_assoc]
      _ = a * b := by rw [mul_inv_mul, mul_inv_mul]
  have h2 : (b⁻¹ * a⁻¹) * (a * b) * (b⁻¹ * a⁻¹) = b⁻¹ * a⁻¹ :=
    calc (b⁻¹ * a⁻¹) * (a * b) * (b⁻¹ * a⁻¹)
        = b⁻¹ * ((a⁻¹ * a) * (b * b⁻¹)) * a⁻¹ := by simp only [mul_assoc]
      _ = b⁻¹ * ((b * b⁻¹) * (a⁻¹ * a)) * a⁻¹ := by rw [← hcomm]
      _ = (b⁻¹ * b * b⁻¹) * (a⁻¹ * a * a⁻¹) := by simp only [mul_assoc]
      _ = b⁻¹ * a⁻¹ := by rw [inv_mul_inv, inv_mul_inv]
  exact (inv_unique h1 h2).symm

(expand the square and slide `e` past `a * a⁻¹` with
`idempotent_mul_comm`). -/
theorem isIdempotentElem_conj {e : S} (he : IsIdempotentElem e) (a : S) :
    IsIdempotentElem (a⁻¹ * (e * a)) := by
  have hcomm := idempotent_mul_comm (isIdempotentElem_mul_inv a) he
  change (a⁻¹ * (e * a)) * (a⁻¹ * (e * a)) = a⁻¹ * (e * a)
  calc (a⁻¹ * (e * a)) * (a⁻¹ * (e * a))
      = a⁻¹ * (e * (a * a⁻¹) * e) * a := by simp only [mul_assoc]
    _ = a⁻¹ * ((a * a⁻¹) * e * e) * a := by rw [← hcomm]
    _ = a⁻¹ * ((a * a⁻¹) * (e * e)) * a := by rw [mul_assoc (a * a⁻¹) e e]
    _ = a⁻¹ * ((a * a⁻¹) * e) * a := by rw [he.eq]
    _ = a⁻¹ * (e * (a * a⁻¹)) * a := by rw [hcomm]
    _ = a⁻¹ * (e * (a * a⁻¹ * a)) := by simp only [mul_assoc]
    _ = a⁻¹ * (e * a) := by rw [mul_inv_mul]

/-- If `a = e * b` with `e` idempotent, then `a = a * a⁻¹ * b`: the defining
equation of the natural partial order only needs *some* idempotent witness. -/
private theorem eq_idem_mul_aux {a b e : S} (he : IsIdempotentElem e) (hae : a = e * b) :
    a = a * a⁻¹ * b := by
  have hinv : a⁻¹ = b⁻¹ * e := by rw [hae, mul_inv_rev, inv_idem he]
  rw [hinv, hae]
  calc e * b
      = e * e * (b * b⁻¹ * b) := by rw [he.eq, mul_inv_mul]
    _ = e * (e * (b * b⁻¹)) * b := by simp only [mul_assoc]
    _ = e * (b * b⁻¹ * e) * b := by rw [idempotent_mul_comm he (isIdempotentElem_mul_inv b)]
    _ = e * b * (b⁻¹ * e) * b := by simp only [mul_assoc]

/-- From `a = a * a⁻¹ * b` derive the mirror equation `a = b * (a⁻¹ * a)`
(slide the idempotents `a * a⁻¹` and `b * b⁻¹` past each other). -/
private theorem eq_mul_inv_mul_aux {a b : S} (hab : a = a * a⁻¹ * b) :
    a = b * (a⁻¹ * a) := by
  have hinv : a⁻¹ = b⁻¹ * (a * a⁻¹) := by
    conv_lhs => rw [hab]
    rw [mul_inv_rev, inv_idem (isIdempotentElem_mul_inv a)]
  have hcomm := idempotent_mul_comm (isIdempotentElem_mul_inv b) (isIdempotentElem_mul_inv a)
  symm
  calc b * (a⁻¹ * a)
      = b * (b⁻¹ * (a * a⁻¹) * a) := by conv_lhs => rw [hinv]
    _ = b * b⁻¹ * (a * a⁻¹ * a) := by simp only [mul_assoc]
    _ = b * b⁻¹ * a := by rw [mul_inv_mul]
    _ = b * b⁻¹ * (a * a⁻¹ * b) := by conv_lhs => rw [hab]
    _ = b * b⁻¹ * (a * a⁻¹) * b := by simp only [mul_assoc]
    _ = a * a⁻¹ * (b * b⁻¹) * b := by rw [hcomm]
    _ = a * a⁻¹ * (b * b⁻¹ * b) := by simp only [mul_assoc]
    _ = a * a⁻¹ * b := by rw [mul_inv_mul]
    _ = a := hab.symm

/-- Transitivity of the defining equation: the composite idempotent witness is
`(a * a⁻¹) * (b * b⁻¹)`. -/
private theorem le_trans_aux {a b c : S} (hab : a = a * a⁻¹ * b) (hbc : b = b * b⁻¹ * c) :
    a = a * a⁻¹ * c := by
  have he : IsIdempotentElem (a * a⁻¹ * (b * b⁻¹)) :=
    isIdempotentElem_mul (isIdempotentElem_mul_inv a) (isIdempotentElem_mul_inv b)
  refine eq_idem_mul_aux he ?_
  calc a = a * a⁻¹ * b := hab
    _ = a * a⁻¹ * (b * b⁻¹ * c) := by rw [← hbc]
    _ = a * a⁻¹ * (b * b⁻¹) * c := by simp only [mul_assoc]

/-- Antisymmetry of the defining equation. -/
private theorem le_antisymm_aux {a b : S} (hab : a = a * a⁻¹ * b) (hba : b = b * b⁻¹ * a) :
    a = b :=
  calc a = b * (a⁻¹ * a) := eq_mul_inv_mul_aux hab
    _ = b * b⁻¹ * a * (a⁻¹ * a) := by conv_lhs => rw [hba]
    _ = b * b⁻¹ * (a * a⁻¹ * a) := by simp only [mul_assoc]
    _ = b * b⁻¹ * a := by rw [mul_inv_mul]
    _ = b := hba.symm

`a = a * a⁻¹ * b`, i.e. `a` is an idempotent multiple of `b`. -/

  le a b := a = a * a⁻¹ * b

  le_trans _ _ _ := le_trans_aux
  le_antisymm _ _ := le_antisymm_aux

    rw [hf2, he2]

    rw [he2, hf2]

  have h2 : (b⁻¹ * a⁻¹) * (a * b) * (b⁻¹ * a⁻¹) = b⁻¹ * a⁻¹ :=

    rw [← mul_assoc, mul_inv_mul]

/-- `a⁻¹ * a` is idempotent. -/

  show a⁻¹ * a * (a⁻¹ * a) = a⁻¹ * a by
    rw [← mul_assoc, inv_mul_inv]

/-- An idempotent is its own inverse. -/
theorem inv_idem {e : S} (he : IsIdempotentElem e) : e⁻¹ = e := by
  have h : e * e * e = e := by rw [he.eq, he.eq]
  exact (inv_unique h h).symm

/-- The product of two idempotents is idempotent (Howie, Thm 5.1.1, first
half): with `x := (e * f)⁻¹`, the element `f * x * e` is an idempotent
inverse of `e * f`, so `x = f * x * e` by uniqueness, `x` is idempotent, and

  obtain ⟨x, hx⟩ : ∃ x : S, x = (e * f)⁻¹ := ⟨_, rfl⟩
  have he2 : ∀ z : S, e * (e * z) = e * z := fun z => by rw [← mul_assoc, he.eq]
  have hf2 : ∀ z : S, f * (f * z) = f * z := fun z => by rw [← mul_assoc, hf.eq]
  have hx1 : (e * f) * x * (e * f) = e * f := by rw [hx]; exact mul_inv_mul (e * f)
  have hx2 : ∀ z : S, x * (e * (f * (x * z))) = x * z := fun z => by
    have h := congrArg (· * z) (inv_mul_inv (e * f))
    rw [← hx] at h
    simpa only [mul_assoc] using h
  -- `f * x * e` is an inverse of `e * f` ...
  have hA : (e * f) * (f * x * e) * (e * f) = e * f := by
    have h := hx1
    simp only [mul_assoc] at h ⊢
    rw [hf2, he2]
    exact h
  have hB : (f * x * e) * (e * f) * (f * x * e) = f * x * e := by
    simp only [mul_assoc]
    rw [he2, hf2, hx2]
  -- ... so it equals `x` by uniqueness, and hence `x` is idempotent
  have hxeq : f * x * e = x := (inv_unique hA hB).trans hx.symm
  have hxx : IsIdempotentElem x := by
    have h : (f * x * e) * (f * x * e) = f * x * e := by
      simp only [mul_assoc]
      rw [hx2]
    rw [hxeq] at h
    exact h
  -- finally `e * f = x⁻¹ = x` is idempotent
  have hef : e * f = x := by
    have h := inv_idem hxx
    rw [hx, inv_inv] at h
    rw [hx]
    exact h
  rw [hef]
  exact hxx

a regular semigroup has unique inverses iff its idempotents commute.

`isIdempotentElem_mul`, and each is then an inverse of the other, so
uniqueness gives `f * e = (e * f)⁻¹ = e * f`. -/
theorem idempotent_mul_comm {e f : S} (he : IsIdempotentElem e)
    (hf : IsIdempotentElem f) : e * f = f * e := by
  have hef := isIdempotentElem_mul he hf
  have hfe := isIdempotentElem_mul hf he
  have he2 : ∀ z : S, e * (e * z) = e * z := fun z => by rw [← mul_assoc, he.eq]
  have hf2 : ∀ z : S, f * (f * z) = f * z := fun z => by rw [← mul_assoc, hf.eq]
  have hA : (e * f) * (f * e) * (e * f) = e * f := by
    have h := hef.eq
    simp only [mul_assoc] at h ⊢
    rw [hf2, he2]
    exact h
  have hB : (f * e) * (e * f) * (f * e) = f * e := by
    have h := hfe.eq
    simp only [mul_assoc] at h ⊢
    rw [he2, hf2]
    exact h
  exact ((inv_unique hA hB).trans (inv_idem hef)).symm

/-- The inverse of a product: `b⁻¹ * a⁻¹` is an inverse of `a * b` (sliding
the idempotents `b * b⁻¹` and `a⁻¹ * a` past each other with

theorem mul_inv_rev (a b : S) : (a * b)⁻¹ = b⁻¹ * a⁻¹ := by
  have hcomm := idempotent_mul_comm (isIdempotentElem_mul_inv b) (isIdempotentElem_inv_mul a)
  have h1 : (a * b) * (b⁻¹ * a⁻¹) * (a * b) = a * b :=
    calc (a * b) * (b⁻¹ * a⁻¹) * (a * b)
        = a * ((b * b⁻¹) * (a⁻¹ * a)) * b := by simp only [mul_assoc]
      _ = a * ((a⁻¹ * a) * (b * b⁻¹)) * b := by rw [hcomm]
      _ = (a * a⁻¹ * a) * (b * b⁻¹ * b) := by simp only [mul_assoc]
      _ = a * b := by rw [mul_inv_mul, mul_inv_mul]
  have h2 : (b⁻¹ * a⁻¹) * (a * b) * (b⁻¹ * a⁻¹) = b⁻¹ * a⁻¹ :=
    calc (b⁻¹ * a⁻¹) * (a * b) * (b⁻¹ * a⁻¹)
        = b⁻¹ * ((a⁻¹ * a) * (b * b⁻¹)) * a⁻¹ := by simp only [mul_assoc]
      _ = b⁻¹ * ((b * b⁻¹) * (a⁻¹ * a)) * a⁻¹ := by rw [← hcomm]
      _ = (b⁻¹ * b * b⁻¹) * (a⁻¹ * a * a⁻¹) := by simp only [mul_assoc]
      _ = b⁻¹ * a⁻¹ := by rw [inv_mul_inv, inv_mul_inv]
  exact (inv_unique h1 h2).symm

(expand the square and slide `e` past `a * a⁻¹` with
`idempotent_mul_comm`). -/
theorem isIdempotentElem_conj {e : S} (he : IsIdempotentElem e) (a : S) :
    IsIdempotentElem (a⁻¹ * (e * a)) := by
  have hcomm := idempotent_mul_comm (isIdempotentElem_mul_inv a) he
  change (a⁻¹ * (e * a)) * (a⁻¹ * (e * a)) = a⁻¹ * (e * a)
  calc (a⁻¹ * (e * a)) * (a⁻¹ * (e * a))
      = a⁻¹ * (e * (a * a⁻¹) * e) * a := by simp only [mul_assoc]
    _ = a⁻¹ * ((a * a⁻¹) * e * e) * a := by rw [← hcomm]
    _ = a⁻¹ * ((a * a⁻¹) * (e * e)) * a := by rw [mul_assoc (a * a⁻¹) e e]
    _ = a⁻¹ * ((a * a⁻¹) * e) * a := by rw [he.eq]
    _ = a⁻¹ * (e * (a * a⁻¹)) * a := by rw [hcomm]
    _ = a⁻¹ * (e * (a * a⁻¹ * a)) := by simp only [mul_assoc]
    _ = a⁻¹ * (e * a) := by rw [mul_inv_mul]

end InverseSemigroup

/-- The **Vagner–Preston map**: right translation by `a`, as a partial

`a⁻¹`. -/
def vagnerMap (a : S) : PartialEquiv S S where
  toFun := (· * a)
  invFun := (· * a⁻¹)
  source := {x | x * (a * a⁻¹) = x}
  target := {y | y * (a⁻¹ * a) = y}
  map_source' := fun x _ => show x * a * (a⁻¹ * a) = x * a by
    rw [mul_assoc, ← mul_assoc a, mul_inv_mul]
  map_target' := fun y _ => show y * a⁻¹ * (a * a⁻¹) = y * a⁻¹ by
    rw [mul_assoc, ← mul_assoc a⁻¹, inv_mul_inv]
  left_inv' := fun x hx => by
    show x * a * a⁻¹ = x
    rw [mul_assoc]
    exact hx
  right_inv' := fun y hy => by
    show y * a⁻¹ * a = y
    rw [mul_assoc]
    exact hy

`elem i a l * elem j b m = elem i (a * P l j * b) m` when the sandwich entry
`P l j` is defined, and `zero` otherwise; `zero` is absorbing. -/
protected def mul : ReesMatrix G I Λ P → ReesMatrix G I Λ P → ReesMatrix G I Λ P
  | zero, _ => zero
  | _, zero => zero
  | elem i a l, elem j b m =>
    match P l j with
    | none => zero
    | some p => elem i (a * p * b) m

/-- `zero` is right-absorbing for `ReesMatrix.mul`. -/
protected lemma mul_zero' (x : ReesMatrix G I Λ P) : ReesMatrix.mul x zero = zero := by
  cases x <;> rfl

/-- `zero` is left-absorbing for `ReesMatrix.mul`. -/
protected lemma zero_mul' (x : ReesMatrix G I Λ P) : ReesMatrix.mul zero x = zero := by
  cases x <;> rfl

/-- The product of two triples is `zero` when the sandwich entry `P l j` is `none`. -/
protected lemma mul_elem_of_none {l : Λ} {j : I} (h : P l j = none)
    (i : I) (a b : G) (m : Λ) :
    ReesMatrix.mul (elem i a l) (elem j b m) = (zero : ReesMatrix G I Λ P) := by
  change (match P l j with
    | none => zero
    | some p => elem i (a * p * b) m) = (zero : ReesMatrix G I Λ P)
  rw [h]

/-- The product of two triples is `elem i (a * p * b) m` when the sandwich entry
`P l j` is `some p`. -/
protected lemma mul_elem_of_some {l : Λ} {j : I} {p : G} (h : P l j = some p)
    (i : I) (a b : G) (m : Λ) :
    ReesMatrix.mul (elem i a l) (elem j b m) = (elem i (a * p * b) m : ReesMatrix G I Λ P) := by
  change (match P l j with
    | none => zero
    | some q => elem i (a * q * b) m) = (elem i (a * p * b) m : ReesMatrix G I Λ P)
  rw [h]

/-- Multiplication in the Rees matrix semigroup is associative. -/
protected theorem mul_assoc' (x y z : ReesMatrix G I Λ P) :
    ReesMatrix.mul (ReesMatrix.mul x y) z = ReesMatrix.mul x (ReesMatrix.mul y z) := by
  rcases x with _ | ⟨i, a, l⟩
  · rw [ReesMatrix.zero_mul', ReesMatrix.zero_mul', ReesMatrix.zero_mul']
  rcases y with _ | ⟨j, b, m⟩
  · rw [ReesMatrix.mul_zero', ReesMatrix.zero_mul', ReesMatrix.mul_zero']
  rcases z with _ | ⟨k, c, n⟩
  · rw [ReesMatrix.mul_zero', ReesMatrix.mul_zero', ReesMatrix.mul_zero']
  rcases hp : P l j with _ | p
  · rw [ReesMatrix.mul_elem_of_none hp, ReesMatrix.zero_mul']
    rcases hq : P m k with _ | q
    · rw [ReesMatrix.mul_elem_of_none hq, ReesMatrix.mul_zero']
    · rw [ReesMatrix.mul_elem_of_some hq, ReesMatrix.mul_elem_of_none hp]
  · rw [ReesMatrix.mul_elem_of_some hp]
    rcases hq : P m k with _ | q
    · rw [ReesMatrix.mul_elem_of_none hq, ReesMatrix.mul_elem_of_none hq,
        ReesMatrix.mul_zero']
    · rw [ReesMatrix.mul_elem_of_some hq, ReesMatrix.mul_elem_of_some hq,
        ReesMatrix.mul_elem_of_some hp]
      congr 1
      simp [mul_assoc]

/-- The Rees matrix semigroup is a semigroup with zero. -/
instance : SemigroupWithZero (ReesMatrix G I Λ P) where
  mul := ReesMatrix.mul
  zero := zero
  mul_assoc := ReesMatrix.mul_assoc'
  zero_mul := ReesMatrix.zero_mul'
  mul_zero := ReesMatrix.mul_zero'
